name: Ragnar Frisch
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: nobelprize.org 1969 economic-sciences summary page names him -- "The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel 1969 was awarded jointly to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen 'for having developed and applied dynamic models for the analysis of economic processes'" -- matching the roster membership URL exactly. ANNOUNCEMENT-YEAR CONVENTION (a5): no Karikó-style offset exists here. The prize's designated year is 1969 and the Stockholm announcement preceded the 10 December 1969 ceremony, so announcement year and designated year are both 1969 and the anchor is unambiguous either way. nobelprize.org has no archived 1969 press release page (the /press-release/ URL 404s into the site shell), so the summary page is cited instead; confidence high because the two readings coincide. a2 (PRIMARY AUTOBIOGRAPHICAL SOURCE): Frisch's own Nobel biographical says "I passed my Ph.D. on a mathematical statistical subject in the Oslo University in 1926." His earlier university degree in economics (Oslo, 1919) and his completed goldsmith's handicraftsman probation (1920) both precede it; the PhD is the last credential completed, so a2=1926. a3: same source, "In 1925 I was appointed Assistant Professor, in 1928, Associate Professor, and in 1931, full Professor in Oslo" -- 1925 is the first paid post in the domain. The 1920 goldsmith qualification is not domain work. a4 unknown: academic career with no founded company, same treatment as p81 Brendle and p105 Gaitsgory. Competing reading noted and rejected: Frisch co-founded the Econometric Society (1930) and founded Econometrica (1933), but a learned society and a journal are not ventures under this frame. a6 unknown: no later qualifying prize; he died in 1973 and the Nobel was his only Nobel/Turing/Fields/Breakthrough award. CLOCK NOTE: a2 1926 to a5 1969 is 43 years, one of the longest education-to-hit spans in the study -- an artefact of the Economics prize being created in 1968, decades after the 1930s work it recognised, not of a slow career.

name: Edward Witten
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster membership URL breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/P1/Y2012 names Edward Witten first among the nine inaugural 2012 Fundamental Physics laureates (Witten, Sen, Seiberg, Maldacena, Linde, Kontsevich, Kitaev, Guth, Arkani-Hamed), under the text "The Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics was founded in 2012 with the naming of nine inaugural laureates". EARLIEST-FIRING PRIZE (a5) -- THE MAIN JUDGMENT ON THIS ROW: the roster drew him off the Breakthrough list, but the frame's prize criterion admits Nobel, Turing, FIELDS or Breakthrough, and Witten took the Fields Medal in 1990, twenty-two years before the Breakthrough. a5 therefore fires on the Fields Medal, not on the list he was sampled from -- the same earliest-firing rule applied to p02 Karikó, whose Breakthrough (2021) was taken over her later Nobel (2023) and the Nobel put in a6. Here the ordering is reversed: Fields 1990 in a5, Breakthrough 2012 in a6. Source for a5 is the IMU's own 1990 Fields Medals page, which lists Drinfeld, Jones, Mori and Witten; Britannica adds that the medal was awarded at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Kyoto in 1990. ANNOUNCEMENT-YEAR CONVENTION: no offset on either prize. Fields Medals are announced at the ICM opening ceremony they are awarded at, so announcement and designation are both 1990; the inaugural Fundamental Physics Prize was announced during 2012 and designated 2012, so a6 is 2012 on either reading. a1/a2/a3 from Britannica, which is explicit: "(born August 26, 1951, Baltimore, Maryland, U.S.)"; "educated at Brandeis University (B.A., 1971) ... and Princeton University (M.A., 1974; Ph.D., 1976)"; "He held a fellowship at Harvard University (1976-77)". a2=1976 is the last credential completed (the 1971 Brandeis BA was in history, and an abandoned economics graduate stint at Wisconsin produced no credential). a3=1976, the Harvard fellowship, is the first paid post in physics; his pre-physics paid work was political journalism and the 1972 McGovern campaign, which is not domain. a4 unknown: purely academic career, no company founded at any point -- same treatment as p81 Brendle and p105 Gaitsgory. NO COMMERCIAL VENTURE FOUND.

name: Larry Ellison
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster membership URL forbes.com/profile/larry-ellison/ names him and prints "#6 in the world today" with "Self-Made Score: 9", inside the frame's self-made requirement. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- NO EARLIER VENTURE FOUND. Every pre-1977 role is salaried employment, not a founded company: notablebiographies has him a "programmer in California for various companies, late 1960s"; referenceforbusiness has him vice president of research and development at Precision Instruments in 1976; Wikipedia adds Amdahl and Ampex in the 1970s, where "His first project included a database for the CIA". The hit entity is therefore the single continuous company he has always run, under three names -- Software Development Laboratories (16 June 1977), Relational Software Inc. (1979), Oracle Systems Corporation (1983), Oracle Corporation (1995) -- not a later, more famous second venture. rev10 CROSSING = 1983, PINNED, NOT BOUNDED. fundinguniverse (International Directory of Company Histories) gives both ends: "by 1982 the company, then with 24 employees and a mainframe and minicomputer customer base of 75, reported annual revenues of nearly $2.5 million" and, of the first portable RDBMS release, "helped Oracle double revenues to over $5 million in 1983." The 1983 bar is $3,093,715 (rev10 constant 2026), so $5.0M is 162% of bar, 62% clear. Corroboration for the above-bar side: Wikipedia cites the Rosen Electronics Letter of February 1983 projecting fiscal 1983 revenue at roughly $8 million, which would be 259% of bar. MARGIN WARNING -- THE BELOW-BAR SIDE IS TIGHT (UNDER 20%): the 1982 bar is $2,997,425 and the two sourced 1982 figures are $2.5M (fundinguniverse, "nearly") and $2.4M (notablebiographies, "sales of $2.4 million"), i.e. 83% and 80% of bar. Oracle was 17-20% short of the 1982 bar, so if either figure is understated or the fiscal-year boundary (Oracle's FY ends 31 May) shifts revenue across the line, the crossing moves to 1982. a5 confidence is medium for this reason, not because the 1983 figure is doubtful. a2: last credential actually COMPLETED is the high-school diploma. referenceforbusiness: "After graduation from South Shore High School in 1962, Ellison enrolled in courses at the University of Illinois", and lists "attended University of Illinois, 1962-1964; attended University of Chicago, 1964-1966"; Wikipedia confirms he "withdrew without taking final exams after his sophomore year" at Illinois and attended Chicago "for one term", so neither produced a degree. Second source: the South Shore High School (Chicago) Wikipedia article lists him in notable alumni as "Larry Ellison (1962)". a3 BOUNDED 1966-1969, LOW CONFIDENCE: no source pins the first programming job to a year. notablebiographies states the range directly -- "Worked as a programmer in California for various companies, late 1960s" -- and referenceforbusiness closes the lower end by having him in Chicago through 1966. Recorded as a 3-year bound rather than a guessed single year. a4 1977: the Oracle Corporation article states SDL "was established on June 16, 1977, in Santa Clara, California by Larry Ellison, Bob Miner, and Ed Oates"; referenceforbusiness says "In 1977 Software Development Laboratories was founded with $2000, and Ellison, as architect of the idea, held majority ownership." DISCREPANCY NOTED: the Larry Ellison article instead says Ellison "joined" SDL "several months after it was founded by Ellison's supervisor at Ampex, Bob Miner". Either reading puts his first venture in 1977, so the anchor is unaffected. a6 1986: Oracle IPO, 12 March 1986, revenue that year $55.4 million (fundinguniverse). The IPO is NOT used to date the hit -- revenue is documented from three years earlier, which bars the fallback anyway.

name: Victor Ho
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster URL ycombinator.com/companies/fivestars names Victor Ho as Founder/CEO alongside Matt Doka (Founder/CTO), batch Winter 2011, founded 2010, description "Customer loyalty and payments platform for small businesses." SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- NO EARLIER VENTURE FOUND. Wikipedia, the Berkeley Founders' Pledge interview, purposenation.org and the YC profile all give the same pre-Fivestars sequence and it is entirely salaried: Goldman Sachs, then McKinsey & Company (customer-loyalty consulting for Macy's and Starbucks per Forbes, 9 Oct 2012), then Fivestars. No company founded before December 2010. rev10 BOUNDED 2010-2016, span 6 years, both ends sourced -- FALLBACK BARRED. Fivestars never IPO'd and was acquired in 2021; the acq50 fallback is barred because sources put it at meaningful scale years earlier. LOWER END: the frame's founding-year rule -- the YC profile dates founding to 2010 and Wikipedia to "In December 2010 Ho launched FiveStars with Matt Doka", so it cannot have earned before then. UPPER END: TechCrunch, 22 Jan 2016, reports "some 10,000 merchants across the U.S. and Canada are using FiveStars' loyalty services"; TechCrunch (25 Sep 2014) and VentureBeat (25 Sep 2014) both state the subscription price directly -- "Merchants pay a flat fee of $200 per month" / "The premium service costs $200 per month". 10,000 x $200 x 12 = $24.0M against a 2016 rev10 bar of $7,454,953, i.e. 322% of bar, so the crossing is above the bar in 2016 with more than 3x of slack -- it clears even if only a third of those merchants paid the premium tier. QUALITATIVE-CLAIM FLAG: no company-published revenue figure exists for any year, so the upper end rests on a merchant-count-times-published-price product plus Ho's own scale statement, not on a disclosed dollar figure. Ho told TechCrunch in September 2014, at 5,300 merchants, "We went from zero to high millions in two years, and we're tripling year over year" -- on that quote alone the crossing is more likely 2014 (5,300 x $200 x 12 = $12.7M vs a 2014 bar of $7,353,351) than 2016, but "high millions" is too vague to pin a year on, so the wider, better-evidenced bound is recorded rather than the narrower, shakier one. The true crossing is probably at the upper-middle of the range, not the 2013 midpoint the clock will use. REJECTED SOURCE: getlatka.com reports "$19.7M revenue" for Fivestars in 2021 but also a "$59.1M valuation" in the same year against a $317M acquisition price two months later, and states its figures are "estimates from public sources and proprietary models" -- not used. a1 unknown: no birth year or age in Wikipedia, purposenation.org, the Berkeley interview or the YC profile after two attempts. The Berkeley interview says he was "22 and 23" at McKinsey, which would imply roughly 1985-1986, but that is an inference and is not recorded. a2 2008: Berkeley Founders' Pledge titles the profile "Victor Ho '08, Co-founder & CEO of FiveStars" -- a UC Berkeley class-of-2008 designation. The degree itself is a triple major in Industrial Engineering, Rhetoric and Business Administration (YC profile, purposenation.org); no graduate degree. a3 BOUNDED 2008-2010 (low conf): sources conflict on the ORDER of his two pre-founding employers. The Berkeley interview says "You worked at McKinsey right out of college" (age 22-23), which puts the domain-relevant job -- customer-loyalty strategy consulting -- at 2008; Wikipedia and the YC profile instead have Goldman Sachs investment banking first and McKinsey after, which would push it to 2009 or 2010. Investment banking is not this bucket's domain, so a3 fires on McKinsey. Lower end is the 2008 graduation, upper end is his departure to found Fivestars in December 2010. a6 2021: SumUp acquired Fivestars for $317M, announced 13 October 2021 (TechCrunch), against a 2021 acq50 bar of $42,083,537.

name: Michael Nusimow
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: the roster URL ycombinator.com/companies/drchrono names Michael Nusimow as Founder/CEO with Daniel Kivatinos as Founder/COO, batch Winter 2011, founded 2009, description "The essential platform for modern medical practices and patients." SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK -- NO EARLIER VENTURE FOUND. His own YC founder bio lists exactly two companies and both are later or the same: "CEO & Founder DrSwarm.com 2026 - Present / Cofounder, CEO DrChrono 2009 - 2022 (YC W2011)". wellfound.com/p/nusimow and me.sh/profile/michael-nusimow (ex-clay.earth) likewise show nothing before DrChrono -- no pre-2009 employer is documented anywhere I could reach, let alone a pre-2009 venture. DrChrono is therefore both his first venture and the hit entity. rev10 BOUNDED 2009-2018, span 9 years, both ends sourced -- FALLBACK BARRED. DrChrono never IPO'd and its 2021 acquisition cannot date the hit, because it was plainly at scale years earlier (Inc. 5000 in 2014 and 2015; ">$3 billion in annual medical claims processed" and 13.2 million patients by December 2018 per the Wikipedia article). LOWER END: the frame's founding-year rule -- Wikipedia, "DrChrono was founded in New York City in 2009 by Daniel Kivatinos and Michael Nusimow", corroborated by the YC profile and by the company's own 2016 press release ("Michael and Daniel started drchrono in 2009"). UPPER END: 2018. FOUNDER-REPORTED FIGURE, FLAGGED: the only dated revenue figure I could find for any year is getlatka.com's "$23M" for 2018 at "6K customers", explicitly attributed on the page to "GetLatka.com interview on Nov 7, 2018 with Drchrono CEO Michael Nusimow" -- i.e. stated by this row's own subject on a dated occasion, not a model estimate. Against a 2018 rev10 bar of $7,799,735 that is 295% of bar, so the upper end survives a very large discount. Confidence medium because Latka is an aggregator rather than a filing or a major publication; note that the SAME source was rejected for p203 Fivestars, where its figure carried no interview attribution and contradicted a known transaction price. Here the attribution is explicit and nothing contradicts it. NARROWER BOUND ATTEMPTED AND ABANDONED: Inc. 5000 would have given a below-bar lower end for 2014 or 2015, but Inc.'s company profile carries no revenue field -- the archived page (web.archive.org/web/20201029055217/https://www.inc.com/profile/drchrono) shows only "3-Year Growth 1,311%", "Year Founded 2009", "Company Size 11-50 employees" and "Inc. 5000 Rankings No. 357 (2015), No. 249 (2014)", with ifc_revenue null in the page JSON. EverCommerce's FY2021 10-K discloses only $21.6M of revenue for ALL five 2021 acquisitions combined, not a DrChrono figure, so it cannot tighten the bound either. The 9-year span is honest rather than convenient. a1, a2 and a3 all unknown after repeated attempts, and a2 is the costly one. Sources reached: Wikipedia (DrChrono), the YC company and founder profiles, wellfound, me.sh, and drchrono's own 2016 Stony Brook 40-Under-40 press release, which states the degree but not the year -- "Michael Nusimow has a B.E. in Computer Engineering & Computer Science from Stony Brook University." me.sh adds a "Certificate of Professional Achievement in Information Systems, Operating Systems, Databases, Networks at Columbia Engineering", also undated, which may be the LATER credential and would be the correct a2 if it could be dated. inc.com and crunchbase.com both refuse automated fetches (DataDome 403), globenewswire.com times out except through the Wayback Machine, and the WebSearch budget for the wave was exhausted before a further route could be tried. No birth year or age is published in any of them; the 2015 "40 Under 40" award implies birth after 1975 but that is an inference and is not recorded. a6 2021: EverCommerce agreed on 2 November 2021 to acquire DrChrono for "approximately $182.5 million" (8-K exhibit 99.1, 16 November 2021; the FY2021 10-K purchase-price table shows $181,919 thousand cash), against a 2021 acq50 bar of $42,083,537.
